findings.claim: The plan never says what 'missing' means for a CLAUDE.md that is a dangling link. The Intent says init writes CLAUDE.md 'whenever it is missing'; r2 says a dangling link is left alone. A dangling link fails is_file() and exists(), so a builder following r1 can treat it as missing and write through it, which is today's bug, or unlink it and write a file, which destroys the user's link. The contract must say: CLAUDE.md counts as missing only when no directory entry exists (os.path.lexists is False); a link, dangling or not, is never replaced. r2's test should cover CLAUDE.md as a dangling link next to a real AGENTS.md, because that is the case that reaches the new write.

With AGENTS.md present, the new CLAUDE.md holds only the block, so the plan rests on an unchecked premise: Claude Code ignores AGENTS.md when CLAUDE.md is absent. If current Claude Code falls back to AGENTS.md when there is no CLAUDE.md, writing a CLAUDE.md that does not import it (an '@AGENTS.md' line) silently drops the user's AGENTS.md instructions for Claude Code. That is a regression the plan does not list. A harness that reads both files (several do) also gets the same block twice. Settle this with a spike: in a repo with only AGENTS.md, does Claude Code load AGENTS.md, and does it load it once CLAUDE.md exists? Then decide what the new CLAUDE.md holds: the block alone, '@AGENTS.md' plus nothing else (one copy for every reader), or both.

The plan reverses a recorded decision but its scope leaves out the record. ADR 0011 (Decision) says 'with neither, it writes CLAUDE.md'. docs/reference/commands.md:57-58, the init help (src/kmctl/__init__.py:63) and the scaffold docstrings say the same. tests/test_init.py test_init_claude_md_replaces_only_the_block asserts that CLAUDE.md does not exist in an AGENTS.md-only repo, so r3 ('any test fails') cannot pass unless that assertion changes, and the plan does not say it may. Name the ADR change (a superseding record or a Correction), the doc and help updates, and the one test whose assertion flips.
"Missing" now means no directory entry (lexists false), so a dangling CLAUDE.md link is never replaced and no CLAUDE.md is written beside it; r2 tests it.
Spike 1 shows Claude Code 2.1.300 loads AGENTS.md only with no CLAUDE.md, and a CLAUDE.md of @AGENTS.md loads it once; the plan writes that import file.
ADR 0011 Correction, help, docstrings, reference and test_init_claude_md_replaces_only_the_block are named; r4 covers the text changes.

A second init run breaks the new import file. After run 1, CLAUDE.md is a real file holding only @AGENTS.md. On run 2, _write_block sees two real files and appends the block to CLAUDE.md, so Claude Code loads the block twice (once by import, once from CLAUDE.md) and init is no longer a no-op on rerun. The plan must say a CLAUDE.md that imports @AGENTS.md gets no block (the same applies to an operator CLAUDE.md that already imports it), and r1 should run init twice and check nothing changes.

The contract does not say what happens when AGENTS.md is a dangling or outside link and there is no CLAUDE.md. CLAUDE.md is "missing" under the new rule, but the block cannot go into AGENTS.md. Writing CLAUDE.md with the block hides the linked AGENTS.md from Claude Code (the harm spike 1 found); writing @AGENTS.md loads no block; writing nothing leaves no block anywhere. Pick one and add it to r2.
Missing means no directory entry (lexists false), so a dangling CLAUDE.md link is never replaced and no CLAUDE.md is written beside it; r2 tests it.
Spike 1 settles the Claude Code 2.1.300 premise: a CLAUDE.md hides AGENTS.md unless it imports it, and @AGENTS.md loads it once.
The ADR 0011 Correction, help, docstrings, reference and the changed test are named; r4 checks the text changes.

The plan now says a CLAUDE.md with an @AGENTS.md line, while AGENTS.md exists, never gets the block, so a second init changes nothing; r1 runs init twice and fails if CLAUDE.md gets the block or any file changes.

The plan picks an outcome for an unsafe AGENTS.md link with no CLAUDE.md: init writes no CLAUDE.md and warns to fix the link and rerun; r2 fails if a CLAUDE.md is written or the warning does not name AGENTS.md.

has_agents uses os.path.lexists, so an AGENTS.md that exists but is not a regular file (a directory) makes init write a CLAUDE.md holding only @AGENTS.md, with no block anywhere and no warning; before this change that repository got a CLAUDE.md with the block. A CLAUDE.md that imports @AGENTS.md beside such an AGENTS.md is likewise skipped in silence. Gate the import case on AGENTS.md being a file (or warn when it is not).

entries.change: An AGENTS.md that is not a regular file (and not an unsafe link) counts as absent with a warning, so CLAUDE.md gets the block instead of an import that loads nothing, and an importing CLAUDE.md beside it is not skipped silently.
An AGENTS.md folder gives CLAUDE.md the block and a warning, alone and beside a CLAUDE.md that imports it.

findings.claim: an AGENTS.md that is a folder or other non-file got a silent @AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md
